slides.0.title: Level 2 Final Assessment
slides.0.subtitle: Test your knowledge of Portugal's key wine regions
slides.0.points.0.label: 10 comprehensive questions
slides.0.points.0.text: Covering Douro・Porto・Vinho Verde・Dão・Bairrada・Lisboa・Tejo・Alentejo・Setúbal・Algarve
slides.0.points.1.label: Level 2 essentials
slides.0.points.1.text: From Port styles to the varieties and winemaking of each major region
slides.1.question: Of the three Douro sub-regions, which is the "core area for top Vintage Port"?
slides.1.options.3: All three sub-regions are equally important
slides.1.explanation: Cima Corgo is the heart of the Douro. Famous top estates such as Quinta do Crasto, Quinta do Vale Meão and Niepoort are concentrated here, and it is the main source of the highest-quality Vintage Port.
slides.2.question: What does the "20 Years" label on a Tawny Port mean?
slides.2.options.0: The youngest wine in the blend is at least 20 years old
slides.2.options.1: All the wine is from a single vintage 20 years old
slides.2.options.2: The average age of the wines in the blend is about 20 years
slides.2.options.3: It must be aged a further 20 years after bottling
slides.2.explanation: The age statements on Tawny Port (10/20/30/40 years) indicate the average age of the wines in the blend, not a specific vintage. The actual blend may contain wines from 5 to 40 years old, and the master blender ensures the final wine matches the style of the stated age category.
slides.3.question: Which is the top Alvarinho sub-region of Vinho Verde DOC?
slides.3.explanation: Monção and Melgaço are the top sub-regions of Vinho Verde DOC. Here Alvarinho is sheltered by mountains and enjoys warmer summers, so it can ripen fully and show the most intense peach and apricot aromas; it is the white wine with the greatest ageing potential in the whole of Vinho Verde DOC.
slides.4.question: Encruzado, the flagship white variety of Dão DOC, is often compared to which famous French white variety?
slides.4.explanation: Encruzado is Dão's flagship white variety. On granite soils and in a cool climate it shows minerality, and after oak ageing it develops creamy, flinty complexity and strong ageing potential. Its style is closest to Burgundy's Chardonnay, earning it the name "Portugal's Chardonnay".
slides.5.question: Bairrada DOC is famous for the Baga variety. What is Baga's most notable characteristic?
slides.5.options.0: Low acidity, rich, for early drinking
slides.5.options.1: High acidity and high tannin, hard to drink young but complex with age
slides.5.options.2: Aromatic and floral, suited to drinking young
slides.5.explanation: Baga is Portugal's variety with the highest acidity and tannin. It is tight and harsh when young, but after 10-20 years of ageing it can show complex aromas of dried roses, leather and mushrooms, and top old vintages can rival Barolo. This is Baga's most important characteristic.
slides.6.question: Why have Colares DOC vines never needed grafting, and still grow on their own roots?
slides.6.options.2: Phylloxera cannot survive in the dune sand
slides.6.explanation: Colares vines are planted in the deep dunes of the Atlantic coast. Phylloxera cannot survive in loose sand, so Colares was never hit by the 19th-century phylloxera epidemic and preserved its precious ungrafted, own-rooted old vines.
slides.7.question: Which of the eight Alentejo DOC sub-regions is known as "the coolest, highest (500-800m) and a source of quality whites"?
slides.7.explanation: Portalegre is Alentejo's northernmost and highest (500-800m) sub-region. Mountain influence gives a cooler climate, and its granite soils give minerality. In recent years it has become a rising star for Alentejo's quality whites, in sharp contrast to the other, hotter sub-regions.
slides.8.question: What is the unique step in Moscatel de Setúbal winemaking that most distinguishes it from other Portuguese fortified wines?
slides.8.options.0: Drying the grapes in the sun before fermentation
slides.8.options.1: Steeping fresh grape skins for 3-6 months before bottling to add Muscat floral aromas
slides.8.options.2: A heating and oxidation process (similar to Madeira)
slides.8.explanation: The unique process in Moscatel de Setúbal is that, after fortification and before bottling, fresh Moscatel grape skins are added to the wine and left to macerate for 3-6 months, greatly intensifying the Muscat floral aromas. This step is not used in other Portuguese fortified sweet wines (Port, Madeira).
slides.9.question: What is the fundamental difference between Madeira's "Canteiro" and "Estufagem" processes?
slides.9.options.0: Canteiro uses added glucose for sweetness, Estufagem does not
slides.9.options.1: Canteiro is natural heated ageing in the upper floors of the lodge (top quality); Estufagem is industrial heating in stainless steel tanks (≤50°C)
slides.9.options.2: Canteiro is completed faster than Estufagem
slides.9.options.3: Canteiro is used only for Sercial, Estufagem only for Malvasia
slides.9.explanation: Canteiro is the natural heating method for top Madeira: casks are stored in the upper floors of the lodge and mature naturally in the Atlantic climate, over as long as several decades, giving more complex and refined quality. Estufagem is the industrial method, heating in stainless steel tanks (maximum 50°C) for at least 3 months, used for high-volume wines.
slides.10.question: How many DOCs does the Algarve have, and which is the easternmost?
slides.10.explanation: The Algarve has four DOCs, from west to east: Lagos・Portimão・Lagoa・Tavira. Tavira is the easternmost DOC, close to Spain and the hottest, driest sub-region, known for Negra Mole and Castelão (Periquita).
slides.11.message: 🎉 Congratulations on completing all of the Level 2 lessons and assessment! You now have in-depth knowledge of Portugal's key wine regions.
slides.11.keyPoints.0: North: Douro (Port on schist terraces)・Vinho Verde (fresh Alvarinho/Loureiro whites)・Trás-os-Montes (extreme continental climate)
slides.11.keyPoints.1: Central uplands: Dão (granite, Touriga Nacional + Encruzado)・Bairrada (high-acid Baga + Espumante)
slides.11.keyPoints.2: Around Lisbon: the nine Lisboa sub-regions・Bucelas (Arinto)・Colares (old vines on dunes)・Tejo (Tagus Valley)
slides.11.keyPoints.3: South: the eight Alentejo sub-regions・Setúbal (Moscatel sweet wine)・the four Algarve DOCs
